intelligence.text: Above Average. Hal Jordan is excellent aircraft pilot, also trained in martial arts and has many years of experience fighting against all manner of foes.

These are powers or abilities that are commonly displayed amongst members of the Green Lantern Corps in order for them to combat their enemies effectively, though do keep in mind not every member shares the same hax these are just the ones that are inherent byproducts of being a member of the Green Lantern Corps...Willpower Manipulation, Emotional Manipulation, Energy Manipulation via Emotional Energy Manipulation (Members of the Green Lantern Corps harness the power of willpower from the Emotional Energy Spectrum in order to fuel their ringsGreen Lantern: Rebirth #3 (February, 2005), it's also stated hereGreen Lantern Vol 5 #21 (August, 2013)), Indomitable Will, Flight, Creation (By using their imaginations members of the Green Lantern Corps can create constructs using their rings, Two-Six states this to be an akin to an equation with an infinite amount of possible outcomes), Telepathy (Members of The Green Lantern Corps can communicate with other members via telepathic sub-channels),

(Team Wide) Universal+ Destructive Capacity via Green Lantern Ring (Any Lantern whom uses a power ring is continuously draining the finite emotional spectrum of their universe which upon emptying ultimately results in the complete destruction of the universe itself, this is stated on multiple occasions) ==Standard Member Paraphernalia== Depending on the skill and willpower of the wearer, it can do almost anything. The first Green Lantern Ring on Earth in modern times was crafted and worn by Alan Scott and powered by the mystical Starheart. His proved to be the exception, the by-product of the efforts of the Guardians of the Universe to contain the magic of the universe. The Guardians also created the more widespread version, powered by individual Green Lantern Power Batteries through a connection to the Central Power Battery on Oa. With the exception of the ring worn by Alan Scott, the current rings are based on the one given to Kyle Rayner when he was the only Green Lantern in existence. All power rings need periodic recharging. The process is not instantaneous so many Green Lanterns recite an oath while the ring charges. The oath is not required to charge the ring, but is recited to reaffirm the person's commitment to the Green Lantern Corps, and to measure the time it takes the ring to charge. While many Green Lanterns create their own oath, the majority use the Corps' official oath as a sign of respect. In the interests of political correctness on the part of DC (or, in context, Hal Jordan), the word "blackest" was replaced by "darkest"; this practice has been abandoned with the reinstating of the Green Lantern Corps due in part to the significance of the Blackest Night comic event. Particularily alien Green Lanterns may have modified oaths. For example, Rot Lop Fan, a Green Lantern from a starless sector, replaces light with sound in his oath. The Central Power Battery is the reservoir of power for the emotional spectrum of willpower, and channels the energy used to empower the Green Lantern Corps. All of the green energy housed within a Green Lantern ring comes from a smaller battery, which in turn, functions as a conduit to the Central Power Battery on Oa. It was built billions of years ago, when the highly evolved Maltusians (now known as the Guardians of the Universe) united their powerful minds to create a green crystal - green because it was a mixture of their blue mental energy and a yellow impurity "necessary to fix its form." They grew the crystal and carved it into the shape of a giant battery, and from the same crystal carved smaller batteries and power rings. The Central Power Battery has been destroyed and rebuilt several times. It was first destroyed several years ago by the forces of Krona. Unfortunately, the battery exploded during an assemblage of all 3,600 members of the Green Lantern Corps, several of whom were killed instantly. The surviving members struggled valiantly to put out the rampaging inferno of green energy that swept across the Oan Citadel. The next cataclysmic event occurred after Sinestro's execution, which resulted in the renegade being imprisoned inside the battery. The energy of the Green Lanterns' power source started to drain their rings, stripping most of them of their power. In the end, it took the combined efforts of Hal Jordan and Appa Ali Apsa to stop the battery from exploding and creating a black hole. However, the damage caused to the battery rendered the Green Lantern Corps almost useless, with only a few Green Lanterns with active power rings scattered throughout the universe.

*Cannot harm anything that is yellow. *Rings only hold a limited energy and must be recharged with a power source on a regular basis. *If the user is filled with dread, they will be unable to use the ring and become vulnerable to the hue yellow. *If Green Lantern loses focus or concentration (for example, due to illusions), his strength weakens. (Basically don't edit my page without my consent) ==Explanations & Related Blog Posts== *Emotional Energy Spectrum: Green occupies the central position in the spectrum and symbolizes the emotion of willpower. It holds the distinction of exerting the least influence on its wielder and can only be mastered by individuals with an indomitable will capable of overcoming great fear. The embodiment of this emotion is Ion. The Maltusians initially harnessed this energy, which later passed on to the Oans, male Maltusians who aspired to establish order in the universe. After the Controllers departed, those remaining on Oa evolved into the Guardians of the Universe. They utilized the green light as the power source for the Green Lantern Corps, an organization committed to combating evil wherever and whenever it emerged to threaten the universe. ==Gallery== *310 Appearances of Green Lantern Corps (Prime Earth) *75 Images that include Green Lantern Corps (Prime Earth) *Organization Gallery: Green Lantern Corps (Prime Earth) ==Others== Notable Victories: Notable Losses: Inconclusive Matches: ==References== ==Categories

field_candidates.value: Low 2-C

These are powers or abilities that are commonly displayed amongst members of the Green Lantern Corps in order for them to combat their enemies effectively, though do keep in mind not every member shares the same hax these are just the ones that are inherent byproducts of being a member of the Green Lantern Corps...Willpower Manipulation, Emotional Manipulation, Energy Manipulation via Emotional Energy Manipulation (Members of the Green Lantern Corps harness the power of willpower from the Emotional Energy Spectrum in order to fuel their ringsGreen Lantern: Rebirth #3 (February, 2005), it's also stated hereGreen Lantern Vol 5 #21 (August, 2013)), Indomitable Will, Flight, Creation (By using their imaginations members of the Green Lantern Corps can create constructs using their rings, Two-Six states this to be an akin to an equation with an infinite amount of possible outcomes), Telepathy (Members of The Green Lantern Corps can communicate with other members via telepathic sub-channels),

(Team Wide) Universal+ Destructive Capacity via Green Lantern Ring (Any Lantern whom uses a power ring is continuously draining the finite emotional spectrum of their universe which upon emptying ultimately results in the complete destruction of the universe itself, this is stated on multiple occasions) ==Standard Member Paraphernalia== Depending on the skill and willpower of the wearer, it can do almost anything. The first Green Lantern Ring on Earth in modern times was crafted and worn by Alan Scott and powered by the mystical Starheart. His proved to be the exception, the by-product of the efforts of the Guardians of the Universe to contain the magic of the universe. The Guardians also created the more widespread version, powered by individual Green Lantern Power Batteries through a connection to the Central Power Battery on Oa. With the exception of the ring worn by Alan Scott, the current rings are based on the one given to Kyle Rayner when he was the only Green Lantern in existence. All power rings need periodic recharging. The process is not instantaneous so many Green Lanterns recite an oath while the ring charges. The oath is not required to charge the ring, but is recited to reaffirm the person's commitment to the Green Lantern Corps, and to measure the time it takes the ring to charge. While many Green Lanterns create their own oath, the majority use the Corps' official oath as a sign of respect. In the interests of political correctness on the part of DC (or, in context, Hal Jordan), the word "blackest" was replaced by "darkest"; this practice has been abandoned with the reinstating of the Green Lantern Corps due in part to the significance of the Blackest Night comic event. Particularily alien Green Lanterns may have modified oaths. For example, Rot Lop Fan, a Green Lantern from a starless sector, replaces light with sound in his oath. The Central Power Battery is the reservoir of power for the emotional spectrum of willpower, and channels the energy used to empower the Green Lantern Corps. All of the green energy housed within a Green Lantern ring comes from a smaller battery, which in turn, functions as a conduit to the Central Power Battery on Oa. It was built billions of years ago, when the highly evolved Maltusians (now known as the Guardians of the Universe) united their powerful minds to create a green crystal - green because it was a mixture of their blue mental energy and a yellow impurity "necessary to fix its form." They grew the crystal and carved it into the shape of a giant battery, and from the same crystal carved smaller batteries and power rings. The Central Power Battery has been destroyed and rebuilt several times. It was first destroyed several years ago by the forces of Krona. Unfortunately, the battery exploded during an assemblage of all 3,600 members of the Green Lantern Corps, several of whom were killed instantly. The surviving members struggled valiantly to put out the rampaging inferno of green energy that swept across the Oan Citadel. The next cataclysmic event occurred after Sinestro's execution, which resulted in the renegade being imprisoned inside the battery. The energy of the Green Lanterns' power source started to drain their rings, stripping most of them of their power. In the end, it took the combined efforts of Hal Jordan and Appa Ali Apsa to stop the battery from exploding and creating a black hole. However, the damage caused to the battery rendered the Green Lantern Corps almost useless, with only a few Green Lanterns with active power rings scattered throughout the universe.

*Cannot harm anything that is yellow. *Rings only hold a limited energy and must be recharged with a power source on a regular basis. *If the user is filled with dread, they will be unable to use the ring and become vulnerable to the hue yellow. *If Green Lantern loses focus or concentration (for example, due to illusions), his strength weakens. (Basically don't edit my page without my consent) ==Explanations & Related Blog Posts== *Emotional Energy Spectrum: Green occupies the central position in the spectrum and symbolizes the emotion of willpower. It holds the distinction of exerting the least influence on its wielder and can only be mastered by individuals with an indomitable will capable of overcoming great fear. The embodiment of this emotion is Ion. The Maltusians initially harnessed this energy, which later passed on to the Oans, male Maltusians who aspired to establish order in the universe. After the Controllers departed, those remaining on Oa evolved into the Guardians of the Universe. They utilized the green light as the power source for the Green Lantern Corps, an organization committed to combating evil wherever and whenever it emerged to threaten the universe. ==Gallery== *310 Appearances of Green Lantern Corps (Prime Earth) *75 Images that include Green Lantern Corps (Prime Earth) *Organization Gallery: Green Lantern Corps (Prime Earth) ==Others== Notable Victories: Notable Losses: Inconclusive Matches: ==References== ==Categories

These are powers or abilities that are commonly displayed amongst members of the Green Lantern Corps in order for them to combat their enemies effectively, though do keep in mind not every member shares the same hax these are just the ones that are inherent byproducts of being a member of the Green Lantern Corps...Willpower Manipulation, Emotional Manipulation, Energy Manipulation via Emotional Energy Manipulation (Members of the Green Lantern Corps harness the power of willpower from the Emotional Energy Spectrum in order to fuel their ringsGreen Lantern: Rebirth #3 (February, 2005), it's also stated hereGreen Lantern Vol 5 #21 (August, 2013)), Indomitable Will, Flight, Creation (By using their imaginations members of the Green Lantern Corps can create constructs using their rings, Two-Six states this to be an akin to an equation with an infinite amount of possible outcomes), Telepathy (Members of The Green Lantern Corps can communicate with other members via telepathic sub-channels),

(Team Wide) Universal+ Destructive Capacity via Green Lantern Ring (Any Lantern whom uses a power ring is continuously draining the finite emotional spectrum of their universe which upon emptying ultimately results in the complete destruction of the universe itself, this is stated on multiple occasions) ==Standard Member Paraphernalia== Depending on the skill and willpower of the wearer, it can do almost anything. The first Green Lantern Ring on Earth in modern times was crafted and worn by Alan Scott and powered by the mystical Starheart. His proved to be the exception, the by-product of the efforts of the Guardians of the Universe to contain the magic of the universe. The Guardians also created the more widespread version, powered by individual Green Lantern Power Batteries through a connection to the Central Power Battery on Oa. With the exception of the ring worn by Alan Scott, the current rings are based on the one given to Kyle Rayner when he was the only Green Lantern in existence. All power rings need periodic recharging. The process is not instantaneous so many Green Lanterns recite an oath while the ring charges. The oath is not required to charge the ring, but is recited to reaffirm the person's commitment to the Green Lantern Corps, and to measure the time it takes the ring to charge. While many Green Lanterns create their own oath, the majority use the Corps' official oath as a sign of respect. In the interests of political correctness on the part of DC (or, in context, Hal Jordan), the word "blackest" was replaced by "darkest"; this practice has been abandoned with the reinstating of the Green Lantern Corps due in part to the significance of the Blackest Night comic event. Particularily alien Green Lanterns may have modified oaths. For example, Rot Lop Fan, a Green Lantern from a starless sector, replaces light with sound in his oath. The Central Power Battery is the reservoir of power for the emotional spectrum of willpower, and channels the energy used to empower the Green Lantern Corps. All of the green energy housed within a Green Lantern ring comes from a smaller battery, which in turn, functions as a conduit to the Central Power Battery on Oa. It was built billions of years ago, when the highly evolved Maltusians (now known as the Guardians of the Universe) united their powerful minds to create a green crystal - green because it was a mixture of their blue mental energy and a yellow impurity "necessary to fix its form." They grew the crystal and carved it into the shape of a giant battery, and from the same crystal carved smaller batteries and power rings. The Central Power Battery has been destroyed and rebuilt several times. It was first destroyed several years ago by the forces of Krona. Unfortunately, the battery exploded during an assemblage of all 3,600 members of the Green Lantern Corps, several of whom were killed instantly. The surviving members struggled valiantly to put out the rampaging inferno of green energy that swept across the Oan Citadel. The next cataclysmic event occurred after Sinestro's execution, which resulted in the renegade being imprisoned inside the battery. The energy of the Green Lanterns' power source started to drain their rings, stripping most of them of their power. In the end, it took the combined efforts of Hal Jordan and Appa Ali Apsa to stop the battery from exploding and creating a black hole. However, the damage caused to the battery rendered the Green Lantern Corps almost useless, with only a few Green Lanterns with active power rings scattered throughout the universe.

*Cannot harm anything that is yellow. *Rings only hold a limited energy and must be recharged with a power source on a regular basis. *If the user is filled with dread, they will be unable to use the ring and become vulnerable to the hue yellow. *If Green Lantern loses focus or concentration (for example, due to illusions), his strength weakens. It holds the distinction of exerting the least influence on its wielder and can only be mastered by individuals with an indomitable will capable of overcoming great fear. The embodiment of this emotion is Ion. The Maltusians initially harnessed this energy, which later passed on to the Oans, male Maltusians who aspired to establish order in the universe. After the Controllers departed, those remaining on Oa evolved into the Guardians of the Universe. These are powers or abilities that are commonly displayed amongst members of the Green Lantern Corps in order for them to combat their enemies effectively, though do keep in mind not every member shares the same hax these are just the ones that are inherent byproducts of being a member of the Green Lantern Corps...Willpower Manipulation, Emotional Manipulation, Energy Manipulation via Emotional Energy Manipulation (Members of the Green Lantern Corps harness the power of willpower from the Emotional Energy Spectrum in order to fuel their ringsGreen Lantern: Rebirth #3 (February, 2005), it's also stated hereGreen Lantern Vol 5 #21 (August, 2013)), Indomitable Will, Flight, Creation (By using their imaginations members of the Green Lantern Corps can create constructs using their rings, Two-Six states this to be an akin to an equation with an infinite amount of possible outcomes), Telepathy (Members of The Green Lantern Corps can communicate with other members via telepathic sub-channels),

(Team Wide) Universal+ Destructive Capacity via Green Lantern Ring (Any Lantern whom uses a power ring is continuously draining the finite emotional spectrum of their universe which upon emptying ultimately results in the complete destruction of the universe itself, this is stated on multiple occasions) ==Standard Member Paraphernalia== Depending on the skill and willpower of the wearer, it can do almost anything. The first Green Lantern Ring on Earth in modern times was crafted and worn by Alan Scott and powered by the mystical Starheart. His proved to be the exception, the by-product of the efforts of the Guardians of the Universe to contain the magic of the universe. The Guardians also created the more widespread version, powered by individual Green Lantern Power Batteries through a connection to the Central Power Battery on Oa. With the exception of the ring worn by Alan Scott, the current rings are based on the one given to Kyle Rayner when he was the only Green Lantern in existence. All power rings need periodic recharging. The process is not instantaneous so many Green Lanterns recite an oath while the ring charges. The oath is not required to charge the ring, but is recited to reaffirm the person's commitment to the Green Lantern Corps, and to measure the time it takes the ring to charge. While many Green Lanterns create their own oath, the majority use the Corps' official oath as a sign of respect. In the interests of political correctness on the part of DC (or, in context, Hal Jordan), the word "blackest" was replaced by "darkest"; this practice has been abandoned with the reinstating of the Green Lantern Corps due in part to the significance of the Blackest Night comic event. Particularily alien Green Lanterns may have modified oaths. For example, Rot Lop Fan, a Green Lantern from a starless sector, replaces light with sound in his oath. The Central Power Battery is the reservoir of power for the emotional spectrum of willpower, and channels the energy used to empower the Green Lantern Corps. All of the green energy housed within a Green Lantern ring comes from a smaller battery, which in turn, functions as a conduit to the Central Power Battery on Oa. It was built billions of years ago, when the highly evolved Maltusians (now known as the Guardians of the Universe) united their powerful minds to create a green crystal - green because it was a mixture of their blue mental energy and a yellow impurity "necessary to fix its form." They grew the crystal and carved it into the shape of a giant battery, and from the same crystal carved smaller batteries and power rings. The Central Power Battery has been destroyed and rebuilt several times. It was first destroyed several years ago by the forces of Krona. Unfortunately, the battery exploded during an assemblage of all 3,600 members of the Green Lantern Corps, several of whom were killed instantly. The surviving members struggled valiantly to put out the rampaging inferno of green energy that swept across the Oan Citadel. The next cataclysmic event occurred after Sinestro's execution, which resulted in the renegade being imprisoned inside the battery. The energy of the Green Lanterns' power source started to drain their rings, stripping most of them of their power. In the end, it took the combined efforts of Hal Jordan and Appa Ali Apsa to stop the battery from exploding and creating a black hole. However, the damage caused to the battery rendered the Green Lantern Corps almost useless, with only a few Green Lanterns with active power rings scattered throughout the universe.

*Cannot harm anything that is yellow. *Rings only hold a limited energy and must be recharged with a power source on a regular basis. *If the user is filled with dread, they will be unable to use the ring and become vulnerable to the hue yellow. *If Green Lantern loses focus or concentration (for example, due to illusions), his strength weakens. It holds the distinction of exerting the least influence on its wielder and can only be mastered by individuals with an indomitable will capable of overcoming great fear. The embodiment of this emotion is Ion. The Maltusians initially harnessed this energy, which later passed on to the Oans, male Maltusians who aspired to establish order in the universe. After the Controllers departed, those remaining on Oa evolved into the Guardians of the Universe. They utilized the green light as the power source for the Green Lantern Corps, an organization committed to combating evil wherever and whenever it emerged to threaten the universe. ==Gallery== *310 Appearances of Green Lantern Corps (Prime Earth) *75 Images that include Green Lantern Corps (Prime Earth) *Organization Gallery: Green Lantern Corps (Prime Earth) ==Others== Notable Victories: Notable Losses: Inconclusive Matches: ==References== ==Categories

field_candidates.value: These are powers or abilities that are commonly displayed amongst members of the Green Lantern Corps in order for them to combat their enemies effectively, though do keep in mind not every member shares the same hax these are just the ones that are inherent byproducts of being a member of the Green Lantern Corps...Willpower Manipulation, Emotional Manipulation, Energy Manipulation via Emotional Energy Manipulation (Members of the Green Lantern Corps harness the power of willpower from the Emotional Energy Spectrum in order to fuel their ringsGreen Lantern: Rebirth #3 (February, 2005), it's also stated hereGreen Lantern Vol 5 #21 (August, 2013)), Indomitable Will, Flight, Creation (By using their imaginations members of the Green Lantern Corps can create constructs using their rings, Two-Six states this to be an akin to an equation with an infinite amount of possible outcomes), Telepathy (Members of The Green Lantern Corps can communicate with other members via telepathic sub-channels),

*Cannot harm anything that is yellow. *Rings only hold a limited energy and must be recharged with a power source on a regular basis. *If the user is filled with dread, they will be unable to use the ring and become vulnerable to the hue yellow. *If Green Lantern loses focus or concentration (for example, due to illusions), his strength weakens. (Basically don't edit my page without my consent) ==Explanations & Related Blog Posts== *Emotional Energy Spectrum: Green occupies the central position in the spectrum and symbolizes the emotion of willpower. It holds the distinction of exerting the least influence on its wielder and can only be mastered by individuals with an indomitable will capable of overcoming great fear. The embodiment of this emotion is Ion. The Maltusians initially harnessed this energy, which later passed on to the Oans, male Maltusians who aspired to establish order in the universe. After the Controllers departed, those remaining on Oa evolved into the Guardians of the Universe. They utilized the green light as the power source for the Green Lantern Corps, an organization committed to combating evil wherever and whenever it emerged to threaten the universe. ==Gallery== *310 Appearances of Green Lantern Corps (Prime Earth) *75 Images that include Green Lantern Corps (Prime Earth) *Organization Gallery: Green Lantern Corps (Prime Earth) ==Others== Notable Victories: Notable Losses: Inconclusive Matches: ==References== ==Categories

Rings hold a limited charge, and need to be recharged with a power battery every so often, cannot be used without strong enough willpower, if the user has too much fear then they are unable to affect things colored yellow. If the GL loses focus or concentration their power will weaken (this can be accomplished via illusions and telepathic attacks, if said GL is unprepared for such things.) Notable Attacks/Techniques: *Auto-aura: A passive ability that activates several enhancements simply by wearing the ring. Grants some increase in durability, regulates temperature and oxygen, allowing the wielder to survive in space. Allows for flight. *Autoshields: A forcefield that activates automatically whenever a GL is in danger, independent of their own will. Superhuman Physical Characteristics, Weapon Mastery (Possesses the skills of many of her previous lives, as well as her own. Also skilled in the usage of gunsDark Nights: Metal Ch 4), Acrobatics (Even without the empowerment of Nth Metal, she could easily perform acrobatic jumps in the middle of intense fights), Vehicular Mastery (Piloted a ship when sunk to microscopic sizes to protect Martian Manhunter's nervous systemJustice League Vol 4 3), Flight and Spaceflight (Shown hereJustice League Vol 4 65), Energy Manipulation and Absorption (Nth Metal works by conducting mystical energyDark Days: The Forge. It can absorb energy attacks and be used to strike back with the same powerDark Nights: Metal Ch 5), Regeneration (Low-Mid. Carter Hall's body heals faster thanks to the Nth Metal's properties, quickly healing all wounds he'd suffered at the hands of Hawkwoman, and Kendra should share this ability as it is bestowed by his Nth MetalHawkman Vol 5 19), Vibration Manipulation (Nth Metal can cause shockwaves when clashing with other Nth MetalHawkman Vol 5 27), limited Physics Manipulation (Structures built of Nth Metal are said to defy the laws of physicsJustice League Vol 4 14), Non-Physical Interaction (Nth Metal can hurt ghostsBatman Eternal 24), Invulnerability Negation (Nth Metal is one of the only things that can nullify the invulnerability of Dark Multiverse beingsDark Nights: Metal Ch 3), Regeneration Nullification (High-Mid. The Nth metal prevented some alien creatures from regenerating, whereas previously they could grow back from just a detached head.Savage Hawkman Vol 1 1 This nullification happens on the cellular levelSavage Hawkman Vol 1 2), Limited Power Nullification (Nth Metal caused Morphicius' teleportation to fail, and then he used it to hinder Katar's flight abilities. It also cancelled a century-long spellSavage Hawkman Vol 1 6), Limited Empowerment (The Nth Metal armor allowed Katar Hol to fight even when he'd otherwise collapse.Savage Hawkman Vol 1 10 It is also the source of Hawkgirl's superhuman strength), Resistance to Poison Manipulation, Mind Manipulation and Morality Manipulation (Hawkgirl overcame a dose of Joker's venom.Justice League Vol 4 6 Carter's Nth Armor slowed down the effect of The Batman Who Laughs's venom meant to turn him evilHawkman Vol 5 20 by suppressing his consciousness in favor of Sky Tyrant'sHawkman Vol 5 21 and eventually overpowered itHawkman Vol 5 23), Disease Manipulation (Former incarnations of Hawkgirl as well as Hawkman's were immune to the plague), Life Manipulation and Absorption (Absorbing Hawkgirl's life essence is painful and difficult because of the Nth Metal's properties. Also, each of the many reincarnations she lived through resides within her, and will be affected before he isHawkman Vol 5 26), Telepathy and Mind Manipulation (Was trained by Martian Manhunter to resist mental attacksJustice League Vol 4 56)

At least Town level (Comparable to Hawkwoman,Justice League Vol 4 15 who defeated Sky Tyrant who caused a shockwave of this size, albeit she lost to her when she had the help of a failed copy of Katar HolJustice League Vol 4 16), Low Complex Multiverse level at peak (Fought Lex Luthor's warsuit.Justice League Vol 4 7 Hurt an off-guard Martian Manhunter.Justice League Vol 4 9 Seemingly injured Gorilla Grodd.Justice League Vol 4 57 Hurt Zumbado, a being who could contend with Black Adam and Aquaman and is an enemy of Naomi.Justice League Vol 4 59 Comparable to Katar HolThe Savage Hawkman Vol 1 15)
Massively FTL+

At least Town level, Low Complex Multiverse level with Nth Metal (Nth Metal is superior to the Eight Metal that gods use for their weapons and armor, such as those used by Wonder Woman. However do note that Hawkgirl's armor only offers partial protection from attacks of comparable foes)
At least Peak Human. Capable of fighting through long battles, and her Nth Metal can allow her to fight even when she'd normally collapse.
Extended Melee Range, Tens of Meters by throwing her mace
Nth Metal Armor and Mace, Optional
Gifted. A skilled combatant who brings the experience of many of her previous incarnations into battle.
At least 9-A physically, 5-A with her Mace, higher with Mace Throw

Superhuman Physical Characteristics (See Attack Potency, Speed, Lifting Strength, and Durability), Flight (Can use her wings to fly at tremendous speeds, and demonstrates great expertise in flight - such as weaving between laser blasts from the Martian Killers, evading a pursuing spaceship, dancing around WW2-era fighter planes, avoiding falling debris while flying out of a collapsing cavern, etc. Dwayne McDuffie, one of JLU’s head writers, went as far as to call Hawkgirl a “world-class aerial combatant”), Genius Intelligence (See Intelligence), Superhuman Athleticism (Leapt to the top of a small flight of stairs from a standing position), Hand-to-Hand Combat Mastery (Was one of the foremost warriors on Thanagar, a belligerent world, with Dwayne McDuffie referring to Shayera as having undergone “the Thanagarian equivalent of Navy Seal training.” Was able to hold her own against the extremely skilled Wonder Woman despite a notable strength gap by utilizing her combat expertise during "Grudge Match." Beat up highly trained Green Lanterns without using her mace. Countered blows from and smacked away Tsukuri, a mercenary with presumable CQC training. Was able to competently fight with her hands bound), Weapon Mastery (with her Mace, which she used with such great proficiency that she rose to a high rank in Thanagar's military, and she was capable of holding her own in weapon combat against Tsukuri, a swordswoman with great enough mastery that Aresia specifically hired her as an enforcer and stopping a mace strike an inch from someone's face. Her signature moves with her mace are throwing it for a long-range attack and spinning it to block attacks), Acrobatics (Did flips to recover from attacks during "Grudge Match" as well as to recover from a kick from Grodd during "Secret Society" and evade an explosion in "Hunter's Moon"), Attack Reflection (Redirected Doctor Fate’s beam with her mace. Sent Mongul's cannon beam back into the cannon from which it came), Electricity Manipulation (Can electrocute foes as powerful as Doomsday with her Mace, and its charge can be lowered so that it functions as a defibrillator. Her Justice Lord counterpart's mace could absorb electricity into itself), Energy Projection (In later appearances, is shown firing beams of electricity from her Mace), Shockwave Creation (Her mace strikes create shockwaves with their sheer impact), Stealth Mastery (Snuck up on a mind-controlled Green Lantern), Vehicular Mastery (with a Javelin, and spaceships in general - one of her most notable feats is casually out-dogfighting Kanjar Ro, an experienced spacefarer, as well as avoiding Star Sapphire's energy beams), Limited Teleportation (Can request to be recalled to the JLU Watchtower), Negation of Intangibility (Her Mace's Nth Metal interferes with dimensional shifting), Negation of all Magic (Nth Metal, the material which makes up her mace, naturally negates all magic, regardless of potency), Indomitable Will/, Resistance to Mind Manipulation (Resisted Despero's mental powers with no aftereffects during "Hearts and Minds", which with a similar amount of exposure took control of Katma Tui, a Green Lantern. However, powerful enough Mind Manipulation can take her over, such as the extremely potent Heart of Darkness during "Eclipsed") *Resistance to Mind Reading (As a Thanagarian Soldier, has a mental block in place that makes Martian Manhunter incapable of reading her mind, at least not without pulling out all the stops) *Resistance to Extreme Heat (Was unhurt by being caught in this fiery explosion as well as this explosion. Being struck by flaming skeletons didn't affect her)

At least Small Building Level physically (Upscaling from 0.095 Tons - Knocked Copperhead out in a single punch, with Copperhead being strong enough to down Batman temporarily with a kick. Struggled evenly with Gorilla Grodd, who easily stomped Lex Luthor in a fistfight. Fought and knocked out gorillas with just her legs. Punched Arkkis Chummuck across a bar, sending him through a wall. Ragdolled a scavenger with a kick), possibly far higher (Staggered Wonder Woman with a kick), Large Planet Level with her Mace (Downscaling from 1.03 Ronnatons - Redirected a beam that had the power to destroy a planet - see Note 2. Though certainly weaker than her teammates, with her mace she can still somewhat hold her own against enemies like a bloodlusted, mind-controlled Wonder Woman ("Grudge Match"), Star Sapphire ("Injustice for All"), Sinestro ("Secret Society"), a Lexo-suit wearing Lex Luthor ("Tabula Rasa"), Queen ("Wild Cards"), one of Lexiac's robots ("Divided We Fall"), etc. In addition, she could, despite not leaving any overt damage, cause Lobo a bit of pain with a mace strike to the top of his head, just barely divert attacks from Lexiac's tentacles and over the course of several attacks, manage to destroy one of them (these tentacles being capable of temporarily restraining a struggling Wonder Woman and Martian Manhunter), knock over (though not actually damage) Darkseid with a mace strike, divert a strike from Luthor's mech, which one-shot her and thus should scale to her durability - in summary, she's certainly weaker than her League teammates (other than Batman), but not to such a great extent that she wouldn't share the High 6-A to 5-B scaling that they have (that is to say, she isn't a hundred or a thousand times weaker than them), independent of her planet-busting-cannon feat. During their bar fight midway through "In Blackest Night," she's strongly implied to be at least somewhat comparable to fodder Green Lanterns such as Gallius Zed and Arkkis Chummuck, whom she was confident in taking on, even with their rings. One-shot a huge sea monster. Can smash Brainiac drones. Destroyed Imperium army ships with single attacks. Sent Grundy through a city street and into the sewer below. Tore through Vandal Savage's heavy gun. Her lower-ends (such as doing less damage to a robot than machine guns) are noted, but less consistent than higher ends and thus treated as outliers. See here for my reasoning as to why DCAU Superman is not Low Complex Multiversal), higher with Spinning Mace Throw (Upscaling from 1.03 Ronnatons - Her thrown mace, after she spun it, broke the Lexo-suit's outer armor despite the fact that her normal swings couldn't so much as dent the suit)

Relativistic+ combat speed and reactions (Scaling to 0.53c - Scales to many feats of characters reacting to, dodging and deflecting lantern beams (which move at the Speed of Light), such as keeping up with and parried attacks from a bloodlusted Wonder Woman, who moved this fast whilst deflecting Lantern Beams. Can keep pace with Hro Talak, who could react to and deflect Lantern Beams at close range after they were fired, as well as very consistently tag Shadow Thief, who could dodge lantern beams after they were fired. Speaking of her scaling to Wonder Woman's combat speed, the amazing Amazon was able to deflect both laser beams from Imperium Army Rifles as well as block Laser Beams from an Imperium army ship. Should be somewhat comparable in speed to Static, who reacted to and blocked a light-based laser after it was fired from close range. Swung her mace to deflect the beam from Mongul's planet-busting cannon as it came toward her, smacking it down - this beam would have traveled an interplanetary distance (to Draaga's planet) in what's strongly implied to be a somewhat short timeframe. Parried a bolt of lightning. Intercepted an ICBM in its terminal phase. Wove around machine gun fire while flying, and could also deflect it. Blocked two sword slashes from and landed a Mace Swing on Tsukuri, who could react to and slash at gunfire in midair. Possesses inhumanly quick reactions, according to Dwayne McDuffie. Has blitzed Killer Frost with attacks on two occasions, with Frost having quick enough reactions to react to and freeze fired arrows), with at least Hypersonic+ flight speed (At least Mach 20 - Caught up with an ICBM in its terminal phase. Flew to intercept an artillery shell. Overtook a WW2 fighter plane) - though it does not seem entirely consistent with the rest of her speed scaling, it should be noted that Hawkgirl was capable of moving around in a dimension that was beyond space and time, which could be interpreted as Immeasurable speed.

Varies, at least Small Building Level (Upscaling from 0.095 Tons - Shayera's durability is almost comically inconsistent, as in some instances she can be hurt and staggered by the likes of Black Canary or being slammed into a wall, and other times she can take hits from the verse's herald-tiers like Wonder Woman and Giganta. Even at her lowest ends, though, her durability should scale here due to Newton's third law as well as feats such as tanking this explosion. Being sent through a stone wall by a Manhunter only annoyed her), at most Large Planet Level (Downscaling from 1.03 Ronnatons - At her most durable, she can take several strikes from a bloodlusted Wonder Woman, as well as a slap from Giganta, who is Diana's physical rival and has no incentive to hold back)

Needs to breathe and eat, with the only tie in comics that have statements to the contrary (other than Batman: The Adventures Continue, which has so many continuity issues that it's essentially impossible to argue it's canon) being Justice League Infinity, the Batman and Harley Quinn tie in comics, and specifically the first annual of Batman Adventures. Ergo, I only consider those three comics canon. Note 2: It's true that Nth metal is said to have “energy dampening properties” during Starcrossed, but in the DCAU the only energy it's shown to dampen is magic, with it never being even remotely implied that it negates or weakens non-magical energy it’s hit, such as Lantern Beams, beams from Brainiac drones, this feat should still scale to her swinging strength due to how open to interpretation Nth metal is in the DCAU, as “energy dampening” could, via Occam’s razor, very likely just be Paran Dul referring to how it interferes with Magical energy, something the Thanagarians are aware of and have defenses against due to their history with Icthultu, not a blanket statement that Nth metal dampens every form of energy. Even more consistently, Nth Metal in the main DC continuity is never noted to have any overall energy dampening

Superhuman Physical Characteristics (See Attack Potency, Speed, Lifting Strength, and Durability), Flight (Can use her wings to fly at tremendous speeds, and demonstrates great expertise in flight - such as weaving between laser blasts from the Martian Killers, evading a pursuing spaceship, dancing around WW2-era fighter planes, avoiding falling debris while flying out of a collapsing cavern, etc. Dwayne McDuffie, one of JLU’s head writers, went as far as to call Hawkgirl a “world-class aerial combatant”), Genius Intelligence (See Intelligence), Superhuman Athleticism (Leapt to the top of a small flight of stairs from a standing position), Hand-to-Hand Combat Mastery (Was one of the foremost warriors on Thanagar, a belligerent world, with Dwayne McDuffie referring to Shayera as having undergone “the Thanagarian equivalent of Navy Seal training.” Was able to hold her own against the extremely skilled Wonder Woman despite a notable strength gap by utilizing her combat expertise during "Grudge Match." Beat up highly trained Green Lanterns without using her mace. Countered blows from and smacked away Tsukuri, a mercenary with presumable CQC training. Was able to competently fight with her hands bound), Weapon Mastery (with her Mace, which she used with such great proficiency that she rose to a high rank in Thanagar's military, and she was capable of holding her own in weapon combat against Tsukuri, a swordswoman with great enough mastery that Aresia specifically hired her as an enforcer and stopping a mace strike an inch from someone's face. Her signature moves with her mace are throwing it for a long-range attack and spinning it to block attacks), Acrobatics (Did flips to recover from attacks during "Grudge Match" as well as to recover from a kick from Grodd during "Secret Society" and evade an explosion in "Hunter's Moon"), Attack Reflection (Redirected Doctor Fate’s beam with her mace. Sent Mongul's cannon beam back into the cannon from which it came), Electricity Manipulation (Can electrocute foes as powerful as Doomsday with her Mace, and its charge can be lowered so that it functions as a defibrillator. Her Justice Lord counterpart's mace could absorb electricity into itself), Energy Projection (In later appearances, is shown firing beams of electricity from her Mace), Shockwave Creation (Her mace strikes create shockwaves with their sheer impact), Stealth Mastery (Snuck up on a mind-controlled Green Lantern), Vehicular Mastery (with a Javelin, and spaceships in general - one of her most notable feats is casually out-dogfighting Kanjar Ro, an experienced spacefarer, as well as avoiding Star Sapphire's energy beams), Limited Teleportation (Can request to be recalled to the JLU Watchtower), Negation of Intangibility (Her Mace's Nth Metal interferes with dimensional shifting), Negation of all Magic (Nth Metal, the material which makes up her mace, naturally negates all magic, regardless of potency), Indomitable Will/, Resistance to Mind Manipulation (Resisted Despero's mental powers with no aftereffects during "Hearts and Minds", which with a similar amount of exposure took control of Katma Tui, a Green Lantern. However, powerful enough Mind Manipulation can take her over, such as the extremely potent Heart of Darkness during "Eclipsed") *Resistance to Mind Reading (As a Thanagarian Soldier, has a mental block in place that makes Martian Manhunter incapable of reading her mind, at least not without pulling out all the stops) *Resistance to Extreme Heat (Was unhurt by being caught in this fiery explosion as well as this explosion. Being struck by flaming skeletons didn't affect her)

At least Small Building Level physically (Upscaling from 0.095 Tons - Knocked Copperhead out in a single punch, with Copperhead being strong enough to down Batman temporarily with a kick. Struggled evenly with Gorilla Grodd, who easily stomped Lex Luthor in a fistfight. Fought and knocked out gorillas with just her legs. Punched Arkkis Chummuck across a bar, sending him through a wall. Ragdolled a scavenger with a kick), possibly far higher (Staggered Wonder Woman with a kick), Large Planet Level with her Mace (Downscaling from 1.03 Ronnatons - Redirected a beam that had the power to destroy a planet - see Note 2. Though certainly weaker than her teammates, with her mace she can still somewhat hold her own against enemies like a bloodlusted, mind-controlled Wonder Woman ("Grudge Match"), Star Sapphire ("Injustice for All"), Sinestro ("Secret Society"), a Lexo-suit wearing Lex Luthor ("Tabula Rasa"), Queen ("Wild Cards"), one of Lexiac's robots ("Divided We Fall"), etc. In addition, she could, despite not leaving any overt damage, cause Lobo a bit of pain with a mace strike to the top of his head, just barely divert attacks from Lexiac's tentacles and over the course of several attacks, manage to destroy one of them (these tentacles being capable of temporarily restraining a struggling Wonder Woman and Martian Manhunter), knock over (though not actually damage) Darkseid with a mace strike, divert a strike from Luthor's mech, which one-shot her and thus should scale to her durability - in summary, she's certainly weaker than her League teammates (other than Batman), but not to such a great extent that she wouldn't share the High 6-A to 5-B scaling that they have (that is to say, she isn't a hundred or a thousand times weaker than them), independent of her planet-busting-cannon feat. During their bar fight midway through "In Blackest Night," she's strongly implied to be at least somewhat comparable to fodder Green Lanterns such as Gallius Zed and Arkkis Chummuck, whom she was confident in taking on, even with their rings. One-shot a huge sea monster. Can smash Brainiac drones. Destroyed Imperium army ships with single attacks. Sent Grundy through a city street and into the sewer below. Tore through Vandal Savage's heavy gun. Her lower-ends (such as doing less damage to a robot than machine guns) are noted, but less consistent than higher ends and thus treated as outliers. See here for my reasoning as to why DCAU Superman is not Low Complex Multiversal), higher with Spinning Mace Throw (Upscaling from 1.03 Ronnatons - Her thrown mace, after she spun it, broke the Lexo-suit's outer armor despite the fact that her normal swings couldn't so much as dent the suit)

Relativistic+ combat speed and reactions (Scaling to 0.53c - Scales to many feats of characters reacting to, dodging and deflecting lantern beams (which move at the Speed of Light), such as keeping up with and parried attacks from a bloodlusted Wonder Woman, who moved this fast whilst deflecting Lantern Beams. Can keep pace with Hro Talak, who could react to and deflect Lantern Beams at close range after they were fired, as well as very consistently tag Shadow Thief, who could dodge lantern beams after they were fired. Speaking of her scaling to Wonder Woman's combat speed, the amazing Amazon was able to deflect both laser beams from Imperium Army Rifles as well as block Laser Beams from an Imperium army ship. Should be somewhat comparable in speed to Static, who reacted to and blocked a light-based laser after it was fired from close range. Swung her mace to deflect the beam from Mongul's planet-busting cannon as it came toward her, smacking it down - this beam would have traveled an interplanetary distance (to Draaga's planet) in what's strongly implied to be a somewhat short timeframe. Parried a bolt of lightning. Intercepted an ICBM in its terminal phase. Wove around machine gun fire while flying, and could also deflect it. Blocked two sword slashes from and landed a Mace Swing on Tsukuri, who could react to and slash at gunfire in midair. Possesses inhumanly quick reactions, according to Dwayne McDuffie. Has blitzed Killer Frost with attacks on two occasions, with Frost having quick enough reactions to react to and freeze fired arrows), with at least Hypersonic+ flight speed (At least Mach 20 - Caught up with an ICBM in its terminal phase. Flew to intercept an artillery shell. Overtook a WW2 fighter plane) - though it does not seem entirely consistent with the rest of her speed scaling, it should be noted that Hawkgirl was capable of moving around in a dimension that was beyond space and time, which could be interpreted as Immeasurable speed.

Varies, at least Small Building Level (Upscaling from 0.095 Tons - Shayera's durability is almost comically inconsistent, as in some instances she can be hurt and staggered by the likes of Black Canary or being slammed into a wall, and other times she can take hits from the verse's herald-tiers like Wonder Woman and Giganta. Even at her lowest ends, though, her durability should scale here due to Newton's third law as well as feats such as tanking this explosion. Being sent through a stone wall by a Manhunter only annoyed her), at most Large Planet Level (Downscaling from 1.03 Ronnatons - At her most durable, she can take several strikes from a bloodlusted Wonder Woman, as well as a slap from Giganta, who is Diana's physical rival and has no incentive to hold back)

Needs to breathe and eat, with the only tie in comics that have statements to the contrary (other than Batman: The Adventures Continue, which has so many continuity issues that it's essentially impossible to argue it's canon) being Justice League Infinity, the Batman and Harley Quinn tie in comics, and specifically the first annual of Batman Adventures. Ergo, I only consider those three comics canon. Note 2: It's true that Nth metal is said to have “energy dampening properties” during Starcrossed, but in the DCAU the only energy it's shown to dampen is magic, with it never being even remotely implied that it negates or weakens non-magical energy it’s hit, such as Lantern Beams, beams from Brainiac drones, this feat should still scale to her swinging strength due to how open to interpretation Nth metal is in the DCAU, as “energy dampening” could, via Occam’s razor, very likely just be Paran Dul referring to how it interferes with Magical energy, something the Thanagarians are aware of and have defenses against due to their history with Icthultu, not a blanket statement that Nth metal dampens every form of energy. Even more consistently, Nth Metal in the main DC continuity is never noted to have any overall energy dampening

Please do not edit this page under any circumstance unless you are a moderator or are listed as an Authorized Contributor within the DC Page., displaying a profound regard for life even in the midst of combat, is an example of her unwavering commitment to justice. She freely admits, in Wonder Woman Vol. 1 issue 600, to purposefully reducing the force of her blows in order to prevent killing her opponents. The Wonder Woman Vol. 3 issue 25 illustrates how deeply ingrained this ethos is in the warrior culture of the Amazon, where it is established that killing is not done unless it is absolutely necessary. This idea goes beyond just physical prowess, as Wonder Woman Vol. 3 issue 14 demonstrates when she displays restraint even against opponents who are noticeably weaker than her. Her unwavering compassion and determination to save lives whenever possible are demonstrated in Wonder Woman Vol. 3 issue 15, where she is shown to be committed to non-lethal solutions even when facing formidable opponents such as Captain Nazi. This is shown in a number of incarnations of her character, as even her Post-Flashpoint Self exhibits the same degree of restraint by sparring the lives of mass shooters who had already fired at her and refusing to kill a Minotaur who had just tried to kill her

*Superhuman Physical Characteristics (See Attack Potency, Speed, Lifting Strength, and Durability) *Flight (Can use her wings to fly at tremendous speeds, and demonstrates great expertise in flight - such as weaving between laser blasts from the Martian Killers, evading a pursuing spaceship, dancing around WW2-era fighter planes, avoiding falling debris while flying out of a collapsing cavern, etc. Dwayne McDuffie, one of JLU’s head writers, went as far as to call Hawkgirl a “world-class aerial combatant”) *Genius Intelligence (See Intelligence) *Superhuman Athleticism (Leapt to the top of a small flight of stairs from a standing position) *Hand-to-Hand Combat Mastery (Was one of the foremost warriors on Thanagar, a belligerent world, with Dwayne McDuffie referring to Shayera as having undergone “the Thanagarian equivalent of Navy Seal training.” Was able to hold her own against the extremely skilled Wonder Woman despite a notable strength gap by utilizing her combat expertise during "Grudge Match." Beat up highly trained Green Lanterns without using her mace. Countered blows from and smacked away Tsukuri, a mercenary with presumable CQC training. Was able to competently fight with her hands bound) *Weapon Mastery (with her Mace, which she used with such great proficiency that she rose to a high rank in Thanagar's military, and she was capable of holding her own in weapon combat against Tsukuri, a swordswoman with great enough mastery that Aresia specifically hired her as an enforcer and stopping a mace strike an inch from someone's face. Her signature moves with her mace are throwing it for a long-range attack and spinning it to block attacks) *Acrobatics (Did flips to recover from attacks during "Grudge Match" as well as to recover from a kick from Grodd during "Secret Society" and evade an explosion in "Hunter's Moon") *Attack Reflection (Redirected Doctor Fate’s beam with her mace. Sent Mongul's cannon beam back into the cannon from which it came) *Electricity Manipulation (Can electrocute foes as powerful as Doomsday with her Mace, and its charge can be lowered so that it functions as a defibrillator. Her Justice Lord counterpart's mace could absorb electricity into itself) *Energy Projection (In later appearances, is shown firing beams of electricity from her Mace) *Shockwave Creation (Her mace strikes create shockwaves with their sheer impact) *Stealth Mastery (Snuck up on a mind-controlled Green Lantern) *Vehicular Mastery (with a Javelin, and spaceships in general - one of her most notable feats is casually out-dogfighting Kanjar Ro, an experienced spacefarer, as well as avoiding Star Sapphire's energy beams) *Limited Teleportation (Can request to be recalled to the JLU Watchtower) *Negation of Intangibility (Her Mace's Nth Metal interferes with dimensional shifting) *Negation of all Magic (Nth Metal, the material which makes up her mace, naturally negates all magic, regardless of potency) *Indomitable Will/Resistance to Mind Manipulation (Resisted Despero's mental powers with no aftereffects during "Hearts and Minds", which with a similar amount of exposure took control of Katma Tui, a Green Lantern. However, powerful enough Mind Manipulation can take her over, such as the extremely potent Heart of Darkness during "Eclipsed") *Resistance to Mind Reading (As a Thanagarian Soldier, has a mental block in place that makes Martian Manhunter incapable of reading her mind, at least not without pulling out all the stops) *Resistance to Extreme Heat (Was unhurt by being caught in this fiery explosion as well as this explosion. Being struck by flaming skeletons didn't affect her)

At least Small Building Level physically (Upscaling from 0.095 Tons - Knocked Copperhead out in a single punch, with Copperhead being strong enough to down Batman temporarily with a kick. Struggled evenly with Gorilla Grodd, who easily stomped Lex Luthor in a fistfight. Fought and knocked out gorillas with just her legs. Punched Arkkis Chummuck across a bar, sending him through a wall. Ragdolled a scavenger with a kick), possibly far higher (Staggered Wonder Woman with a kick), Large Planet Level with her Mace (Downscaling from 1.03 Ronnatons - Redirected a beam that had the power to destroy a planet - see Note 2. Though certainly weaker than her teammates, with her mace she can still somewhat hold her own against enemies like a bloodlusted, mind-controlled Wonder Woman ("Grudge Match"), Star Sapphire ("Injustice for All"), Sinestro ("Secret Society"), a Lexo-suit wearing Lex Luthor ("Tabula Rasa"), Queen ("Wild Cards"), one of Lexiac's robots ("Divided We Fall"), etc. In addition, she could, despite not leaving any overt damage, cause Lobo a bit of pain with a mace strike to the top of his head, just barely divert attacks from Lexiac's tentacles and over the course of several attacks, manage to destroy one of them (these tentacles being capable of temporarily restraining a struggling Wonder Woman and Martian Manhunter), knock over (though not actually damage) Darkseid with a mace strike, divert a strike from Luthor's mech, which one-shot her and thus should scale to her durability - in summary, she's certainly weaker than her League teammates (other than Batman), but not to such a great extent that she wouldn't share the High 6-A to 5-B scaling that they have (that is to say, she isn't a hundred or a thousand times weaker than them), independent of her planet-busting-cannon feat. During their bar fight midway through "In Blackest Night," she's strongly implied to be at least somewhat comparable to fodder Green Lanterns such as Gallius Zed and Arkkis Chummuck, whom she was confident in taking on, even with their rings. One-shot a huge sea monster. Can smash Brainiac drones. Destroyed Imperium army ships with single attacks. Sent Grundy through a city street and into the sewer below. Tore through Vandal Savage's heavy gun. Her lower-ends (such as doing less damage to a robot than machine guns) are noted, but less consistent than higher ends and thus treated as outliers. See here for my reasoning as to why DCAU Superman is not Low Complex Multiversal), higher with Spinning Mace Throw (Upscaling from 1.03 Ronnatons - Her thrown mace, after she spun it, broke the Lexo-suit's outer armor despite the fact that her normal swings couldn't so much as dent the suit)

Relativistic+ combat speed and reactions (Scaling to 0.53c - Scales to many feats of characters reacting to, dodging and deflecting lantern beams (which move at the Speed of Light), such as keeping up with and parried attacks from a bloodlusted Wonder Woman, who moved this fast whilst deflecting Lantern Beams. Can keep pace with Hro Talak, who could react to and deflect Lantern Beams at close range after they were fired, as well as very consistently tag Shadow Thief, who could dodge lantern beams after they were fired. Speaking of her scaling to Wonder Woman's combat speed, the amazing Amazon was able to deflect both laser beams from Imperium Army Rifles as well as block Laser Beams from an Imperium army ship. Should be somewhat comparable in speed to Static, who reacted to and blocked a light-based laser after it was fired from close range. Swung her mace to deflect the beam from Mongul's planet-busting cannon as it came toward her, smacking it down - this beam would have traveled an interplanetary distance (to Draaga's planet) in what's strongly implied to be a somewhat short timeframe. Parried a bolt of lightning. Intercepted an ICBM in its terminal phase. Wove around machine gun fire while flying, and could also deflect it. Blocked two sword slashes from and landed a Mace Swing on Tsukuri, who could react to and slash at gunfire in midair. Possesses inhumanly quick reactions, according to Dwayne McDuffie. Has blitzed Killer Frost with attacks on two occasions, with Frost having quick enough reactions to react to and freeze fired arrows), with at least Hypersonic+ flight speed (At least Mach 20 - Caught up with an ICBM in its terminal phase. Flew to intercept an artillery shell. Overtook a WW2 fighter plane) - though it does not seem entirely consistent with the rest of her speed scaling, it should be noted that Hawkgirl was capable of moving around in a dimension that was beyond space and time, which could be interpreted as Immeasurable speed.

Varies, at least Small Building Level (Upscaling from 0.095 Tons - Shayera's durability is almost comically inconsistent, as in some instances she can be hurt and staggered by the likes of Black Canary or being slammed into a wall, and other times she can take hits from the verse's herald-tiers like Wonder Woman and Giganta. Even at her lowest ends, though, her durability should scale here due to Newton's third law as well as feats such as tanking this explosion. Being sent through a stone wall by a Manhunter only annoyed her), at most Large Planet Level (Downscaling from 1.03 Ronnatons - At her most durable, she can take several strikes from a bloodlusted Wonder Woman, as well as a slap from Giganta, who is Diana's physical rival and has no incentive to hold back)

Needs to breathe and eat. Note: Bruce Timm has stated that the original DCAU tie-in comics are not canon, with the only tie in comics that have statements to the contrary (other than Batman: The Adventures Continue, which has so many continuity issues that it's essentially impossible to argue it's canon) being Justice League Infinity, the Batman and Harley Quinn tie in comics, and specifically the first annual of Batman Adventures. Ergo, I only consider those three comics canon. Note 2: It's true that Nth metal is said to have “energy dampening properties” during Starcrossed, but in the DCAU the only energy it's shown to dampen is magic, with it never being even remotely implied that it negates or weakens non-magical energy it’s hit, such as Lantern Beams, beams from Brainiac drones, and the beam of Mongul's cannon - ergo, this feat should still scale to her swinging strength due to how open to interpretation Nth metal is in the DCAU, as “energy dampening” could, via Occam’s razor, very likely just be Paran Dul referring to how it interferes with Magical energy, something the Thanagarians are aware of and have defenses against due to their history with Icthultu, not a blanket statement that Nth metal dampens every form of energy. Even more consistently, Nth Metal in the main DC continuity is never noted to have any overall energy dampening, but specifically dampening of magic and magic alone - with us being given very little reason to believe that the DCAU would take such huge liberties in their adaptation of the material. Even with the Nth Metal failing and without his healing factor, he could keep fighting and running after several arrow wounds.
Extended Melee Range, Tens of Meters by throwing weaponry
Nth Metal Armor

Is not aware of his resurrection abilities and has no memories of any of those previous lives
9-B physically, at least 9-A, possibly far higher with Nth Metal Weapons

Superhuman Physical Characteristics (See Attack Potency, Speed, and Durability), Flight (Can fly with his Nth Metal Wing Harness, with enough finesse to expertly weave around falling debris), Weapon Mastery (Said to wield notable "fighting skills," using his Nth Metal Axe, Spear, and Swords), Paralysis Inducement and Negation of Intangibility (with his Nth Metal Net, which could disrupt Gentleman Ghost's ability to shift through dimensions), Negation of Intangibility and Magic with Nth Metal Weapons (Nth Metal negates all magic, as well as dimensional shifting)

Wall Level physically (Upscaling from 17 Kilojoules - By the time he begins operating as Hawkman, fighting supervillains on a regular basis, considering his athletic build, he should at least be stronger than Doctor Destiny), at least Small Building Level (Upscaling from 0.095 Tons - With his Nth Metal Axe, sliced through the same type of restraint that was being used to handily restrain Hawkgirl. An Nth Metal spear, used by Hawkman, could slice and pierce through mummies which could tank strikes from Batman), very unlikely far higher with Nth Metal Weapons (Carter was capable of slicing apart a solid Shadow Thief's arm, with Shadow Thief's solid parts, as of "Ancient History," being capable of tanking beams from a desperate Green Lantern - however, this would imply that Carter, a human who is shown to be a one-shot-difference weaker than Hawkgirl, can produce greater force by swinging a random sword than Hawkgirl can by swinging an Nth Metal Mace - an idea that is wildly inconsistent and on-its-face ridiculous) - See Note for an explanation as to why I don't think Carter's struggling with Shadow Thief scales him to ST's physicals.

Relativistic+ reactions and combat speed (Scaling to 0.53c - Tagged the Shadow Thief and evenly swordfought with him - Shadow Thief could react to and dodge Lantern Beams (which move at the Speed of Light) after they were fired, and has tagged Batman and Hawkgirl, as well as Vixen. Reacted and weaved around obstacles while desperately flying to save the Absorbacron. Saved Hawkgirl from the fired darts of a booby trap), with Hypersonic+ flight speed (Flew in tandem with Hawkgirl, who had incentive to fly at full speed in order to save Batman from the collapsing tomb)

Wall Level (Upscaling from 17 Kilojoules - Scaling to his AP as per Newton’s Third Law), possibly higher (Taking a half-hearted hit from Shadow Thief isn't really an indisputable durability feat for Carter, because ST has incentive to not do Carter serious harm, as the two are halves of a whole and thus inextricably linked)

Normal Human Weaknesses, Carter is a normal human and his Nth Metal is never referenced as something that enhances his strength. And yet, he's shown capable of physically overpowering Shadow Thief - Shadow Thief being shown capable of casually shattering chains that Hawkgirl couldn't break while attempting to muscle out of and defeating Green Lantern in "Ancient History" - this is at total odds with the fact that Carter is a normal human, and in fact can't even stay conscious after a single hit from Hawkgirl. The obvious rationale for this is that Shadow Thief, who is later revealed to be Carter's literal other half, is likely more susceptible to Carter's attacks than the attacks of others, as Carter could quite literally force ST back into his soul in that same episode. The only alternative explanation is that for some reason, with his bare hands, is substantially stronger than the woman who knocked him out in a single hit prior, as well as equal to or stronger than a Green Lantern Ring. That alternative explanation is, completely ludicrous, and so Occam's razor dictates that Carter cannot be thought of as actually scaling to Shadow Thief, especially not with base physicals. Note 2: Bruce Timm has stated that the original DCAU tie-in comics are not canon, with the only tie in comics that have statements to the contrary (other than Batman: The Adventures Continue, which has so many continuity issues that it's essentially impossible to argue it's canon) being Justice League Infinity, the Batman and Harley Quinn tie in comics, and specifically the first annual of Batman Adventures. Wall Level physically (Upscaling from 17 Kilojoules - By the time he begins operating as Hawkman, fighting supervillains on a regular basis, considering his athletic build, he should at least be stronger than Doctor Destiny), at least Small Building Level (Upscaling from 0.095 Tons - With his Nth Metal Axe, sliced through the same type of restraint that was being used to handily restrain Hawkgirl. An Nth Metal spear, used by Hawkman, could slice and pierce through mummies which could tank strikes from Batman), very unlikely far higher with Nth Metal Weapons (Carter was capable of slicing apart a solid Shadow Thief's arm, with Shadow Thief's solid parts, as of "Ancient History," being capable of tanking beams from a desperate Green Lantern - however, this would imply that Carter, a human who is shown to be a one-shot-difference weaker than Hawkgirl, can produce greater force by swinging a random sword than Hawkgirl can by swinging an Nth Metal Mace - an idea that is wildly inconsistent and on-its-face ridiculous) - See Note for an explanation as to why I don't think Carter's struggling with Shadow Thief scales him to ST's physicals.

Relativistic+ reactions and combat speed (Scaling to 0.53c - Tagged the Shadow Thief and evenly swordfought with him - Shadow Thief could react to and dodge Lantern Beams (which move at the Speed of Light) after they were fired, and has tagged Batman and Hawkgirl, as well as Vixen. Reacted and weaved around obstacles while desperately flying to save the Absorbacron. Saved Hawkgirl from the fired darts of a booby trap), with Hypersonic+ flight speed (Flew in tandem with Hawkgirl, who had incentive to fly at full speed in order to save Batman from the collapsing tomb)

Wall Level (Upscaling from 17 Kilojoules - Scaling to his AP as per Newton’s Third Law), possibly higher (Taking a half-hearted hit from Shadow Thief isn't really an indisputable durability feat for Carter, because ST has incentive to not do Carter serious harm, as the two are halves of a whole and thus inextricably linked)

Normal Human Weaknesses, Carter is a normal human and his Nth Metal is never referenced as something that enhances his strength. And yet, he's shown capable of physically overpowering Shadow Thief - Shadow Thief being shown capable of casually shattering chains that Hawkgirl couldn't break while attempting to muscle out of and defeating Green Lantern in "Ancient History" - this is at total odds with the fact that Carter is a normal human, and in fact can't even stay conscious after a single hit from Hawkgirl. The obvious rationale for this is that Shadow Thief, who is later revealed to be Carter's literal other half, is likely more susceptible to Carter's attacks than the attacks of others, as Carter could quite literally force ST back into his soul in that same episode. The only alternative explanation is that for some reason, with his bare hands, is substantially stronger than the woman who knocked him out in a single hit prior, as well as equal to or stronger than a Green Lantern Ring. That alternative explanation is, completely ludicrous, and so Occam's razor dictates that Carter cannot be thought of as actually scaling to Shadow Thief, especially not with base physicals. Note 2: Bruce Timm has stated that the original DCAU tie-in comics are not canon, with the only tie in comics that have statements to the contrary (other than Batman: The Adventures Continue, which has so many continuity issues that it's essentially impossible to argue it's canon) being Justice League Infinity, the Batman and Harley Quinn tie in comics, and specifically the first annual of Batman Adventures. None Notes: The reasoning behind this character's existence and tiering is the following: Grant Morrison has stated in interviews that, beyond the DC Multiverse and the Monitor-World, only God, the Monitor-Mind, and Jack Kirby's Source exist, and that those three entities's contradictions are resolved into a singular "unity". In addition to this, the fact that the Source and the Overvoid are implied to be the same concept in several different occasions, as well as the fact that the Presence was implied to reside on the same level of existence as the Source several times overall makes it clear that those entities share a common "essence", as outlined by Grant Morrison throughout the aforementioned interview. Additionally, in The Spectre #10 storyline, J. M. DeMatteis seems to heavily point to or confirm such a composite view of God himself, referring to the The Source (herein blatantly treated as the white page the comics are drawn on and referred to as "the void beyond all voids", thus ultimately connecting to Monitor-Mind The Overvoid) and The Presence as a connected "spirit", which he refers to as "The Oversoul", or "The Creator". Note, however, that the above arguments don't necessarily point to those entities as being "lower aspects" or mere avatars of "God", but rather that they are all connected to each other and overall form one singular essence that is both equally as powerful as them and devoid of the Bcontradictions caused by their existence

Various blades, firearms and explosives. *The Deathstroke: It is an antique war blade that Slade won in a poker game. It was later re-cast in Promethium that's capable of absorbing an enormous amount of any kind of energy. *Titanium Staff: His titanium staff can fire powerful energy blasts. Its mode can be switched from "stun to kill", and it can be split into two to produce ultrasonics. Optional

Extraordinary Genius (Despite all of his enhanced physical attributes and healing, Slade's real superpower is his intellect. His strategic genius is arguably superior to Batman. Outsmarted Batman on multiple occasions. Easily saw through a Teen Titan's trap that uses Djinn's magic and had help from Jericho. Batman doesn't even try to understand his real motives. Figured out the true person that sent out Damian Wayne's fake blood test results, while even Batman couldn't. Has eidetic memory, remembered a guy he saw for three seconds a decade ago. Nonchalantly figured out Batman's identity and sneaked up on him, putting a gun to his face. Managed to tap into the Speed Force to gain superspeed, but later lost it after gaining a higher consciousness. Deathstroke enhancements also evolved his brain, granting him an enhanced mental capacity, causing his mind to operate at peak efficiency, nine times beyond that of a normal man.Batman (Volume 3) #86, p. 11 He describes his mind as a super-computer designed to process information and break it down with superior tactical and strategic thought.Deathstroke (Volume 2) #9, p. 7)

He is half blind due to having his right eye shot out before he received his healing factor. Due to him having an Ikon Suit prototype, his left arm isn't fully covered. intelligence.text: At least Genius, possibly Extraordinary Genius. John Constantine is very knowledgeable in ancient and occult matters,Constantine Vol 1 1 such as obscure monsters from various mythologies, not to speak of the many, many spells he is able to use and defuse.The Hellblazer Vol 1 15 Learned how to use Zatanna's backwards magic just by having heard her mumble it in her sleep,Justice League Dark Vol 1 3 while she had to endure years of incredibly rigid training to master it. John's sheer magic skill is such that he could threaten even powerhouses such as The Spectre or Swamp Thing. Was the only one among the Justice League Dark to figure out how to seal June Moon and the Enchantress together and that Madame Xanadu was the one to split them in the first place. Despite the (mutual) hatred that almost everyone in the Justice League Dark has shown towards Constantine, he has proven to be a very good leader, coming up with clever plans and being able to adapt them on the spot.Trinity of Sin: Pandora Vol 1 7Justice League Dark Vol 1 9 Knows all about Shazam's origin and powers.Justice League Dark Vol 1 22 Mostly correctly guessed that The Phantom Stranger was only imitating human feelings. Defeated all the Justice League Dark except Zatanna at once while drunk. Came up with a plan to turn a madman's obsession with William Blake against him. As better detailed in his Social Influencing section in Powers & Abilities, John Constantine is known as the World's Greatest Con Man for a reason, with him having shown the ability to adapt his incredible talking and planning skills to basically any situation, to the point that one could say that despite his wealth of magical knowledge, John's best weapon is his cunning. Standard Tactics: Constantine is typically not a fighter. If possible, he will retreat from a fight to find help or a better strategy. If that is impossible, he is a dirty fighter, sometimes completely forgoing flashy magic spells for more subtle and sneaky tactics if it fits the situation. Other times, he will seek to end the fight as quickly as possible, resorting to techniques that ignore durability in favor of incapacitating or even killing the enemy in some other way.

Defeated all the Justice League Dark except Zatanna at once while drunk. Came up with a plan to turn a madman's obsession with William Blake against him. As better detailed in his Social Influencing section in Powers & Abilities, John Constantine is known as the World's Greatest Con Man for a reason, with him having shown the ability to adapt his incredible talking and planning skills to basically any situation, to the point that one could say that despite his wealth of magical knowledge, John's best weapon is his cunning. Standard Tactics: Constantine is typically not a fighter. If possible, he will retreat from a fight to find help or a better strategy. If that is impossible, he is a dirty fighter, sometimes completely forgoing flashy magic spells for more subtle and sneaky tactics if it fits the situation. Other times, he will seek to end the fight as quickly as possible, resorting to techniques that ignore durability in favor of incapacitating or even killing the enemy in some other way.

Suffers from lung cancer now that his Demon Blood has been removed. Most of his magic has a cost he will eventually have to pay, though this cost will often not be physical, but end up making his life worse by hurting those close to him instead.
